locator: I.16 [3]: Hence, He has no admixture of potency in Himself
interpretation: From act's simple priority (whatever is in some way in potency has something prior to it) and God's being the first being, Aquinas concludes that God has no admixture of potency. Read as the general step that the first being, to which nothing is prior, is in potency in no respect; the step does not depend on which being is first. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
